thread:
sam (support): FYI incoming SEV for a customer on Dedicated — scale-up is lagging, lots of 429s and a couple of 403 attach failures. They see a long delay between request and pod becoming ready.
ryan (eng-runtime): Can you paste a quick timeline and a repro request? is this hitting min_replicas or max_replicas boundaries?
sam (support): Timeline: spike at 09:21 UTC -> probes started at 09:21:12 -> many requests queued -> first 429s at 09:21:30 -> attach 403s at 09:21:45 -> a bunch of pods stuck in Init at 09:22:10. Customer says they have min_replicas=2, max_replicas=20, and policy is burst.
maria (eng-platform): Any recent change to warm-pool config or IAM roles? 403 on attach smells like token/role problem during scale events.
sam (support): No config changes reported by customer. They are on Dedicated US-west. I pulled a control-plane trace and saw many deferred scale requests queued in the autoscaler for ~18s.
ryan (eng-runtime): Can you add the probe logs and the attach error snippet? also which image registry — are we seeing pullbackoff?
sam (support): Logs from the cluster (redacted):
```
attach-controller: authz failure response=403 reason="ServiceAccount token not found" pod=my-customer-pod-7 Init
kubelet: image pull backoff for image=redwood/model:prod-gpu
warm-pool: reserve request queued id=abc123 timeout_ms=12000
```

jess (customer-success): Customer mentions they had a transient billing hold cleared right before the spike — could that cause token rotations to be invalid?
maria (eng-platform): Possibly. If KMS/HSM rotation or billing lock triggers credential revocation, attach controller might fail until new tokens propagate. But that wouldn't explain long autoscaler queueing unless warm-pool capacity was exhausted.
ryan (eng-runtime): Check GPU util and noisy neighbor metrics during the spike. If warm pool was starved (all warm instances attached elsewhere), the autoscaler will enqueue scale requests and backoff.
oncall-bot: Incident created #INC-20262 — assigned to ryan (eng-runtime).
infra-bot: Noted: account quota for attach operations at 380/400 during 09:20-09:23 UTC (spike window).
ryan (eng-runtime): Ok repro hypothesis: billing hold triggered token revoke leading to attach 403s for a subset of attach ops while overall attach throughput hit quota, causing cascading queueing and scale-up delay. Steps to repro: 1) simulate spike with loadgen against dedicated service 2) temporarily revoke service-account tokens (dev env) 3) monitor autoscaler queue and warm-pool attach latencies.
sam (support): Customer asked for immediate mitigation — any quick workarounds?
maria (eng-platform): Short-term: increase warm_pool_min and pre-warm additional capacity for the burst window. Also temporarily raise attach quota if safe. Long-term: add graceful retry + backoff with token refresh and surface clearer errors in console.
ryan (eng-runtime): I'll add a probe to fail fast on attach 403s so scale requests don't pile behind auth failures and we can short-circuit into fallback model variants. Also will instrument autoscaler queue length in dashboards.
sam (support): Noted. I'll relay mitigation to the customer and request logs for the billing hold timing. Thanks. :thumbsup:
jess (customer-success): Customer appreciated the quick plan, will provide the billing event ID and exact timestamps.
ryan (eng-runtime): Follow-up tasks: 1) reproduce in staging (ryan) 2) dashboard for attach-queue (maria) 3) retries/token-refresh patch (ryan) 4) doc for on-call playbook (sam).
sam (support): Closing loop here once staging repro and short-term warm-pool bump are done.
